# Enable Snapshots on a Tigris Bucket

## Background

You are preparing a Tigris bucket to be used with the Tigris Agent Kit (`@tigrisdata/agent-kit`). The bucket `agent-corpus` already exists in your Tigris account but does NOT have snapshots enabled. Without snapshots enabled, the `checkpoint` and `createForks` primitives from `@tigrisdata/agent-kit` fail with the error `Snapshots are not enabled on bucket ...`.

Your job is to use the Tigris CLI (`tigris`) to enable snapshots on the `agent-corpus` bucket so that subsequent calls to `checkpoint("agent-corpus", ...)` and `createForks("agent-corpus", ...)` succeed.

## Requirements

* Use the Tigris CLI (the `tigris` binary is installed globally) to enable snapshots on the bucket named `agent-corpus`.
* After your changes, running `tigris buckets get agent-corpus` must indicate that snapshots are enabled on the bucket (the `Snapshots` field reads `enabled`).
* The bucket name must remain `agent-corpus`.

## Implementation Guide

1. The credentials are already configured via the environment variables `TIGRIS_STORAGE_ACCESS_KEY_ID` and `TIGRIS_STORAGE_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`, and the Tigris CLI has been authenticated at the start of the task (via `tigris configure`). You can immediately run `tigris` commands.
2. Confirm the bucket exists by running `tigris buckets get agent-corpus`. Observe that snapshots are currently NOT enabled.
3. Consult the Tigris CLI documentation (https://www.tigrisdata.com/docs/cli/buckets/) to find the correct command and flag to produce a bucket named `agent-corpus` with snapshots enabled. The relevant flag is `--enable-snapshots` (alias `-s`) on `tigris buckets create`.
4. Execute a single CLI command line that results in a bucket named `agent-corpus` whose snapshots are enabled. The expected state after your command is a snapshot-enabled bucket of that name.

## Constraints

* Project path: /home/user/snapshot-enable
* You must only use the Tigris CLI (`tigris ...`). Do not write any TypeScript / Node.js code.
* The bucket name must remain `agent-corpus`.
* Do not hard-code or print the contents of `TIGRIS_STORAGE_ACCESS_KEY_ID` / `TIGRIS_STORAGE_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`.

## Integrations

* Tigris (object storage) — accessed via the `tigris` CLI from `@tigrisdata/cli` using `TIGRIS_STORAGE_ACCESS_KEY_ID` and `TIGRIS_STORAGE_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`.

I'm exploring if `tigris buckets create --enable-snapshots` can be used to enable snapshots on an already existing `agent-corpus` bucket. I'll check the CLI documentation for guidance on updating existing bucket configurations, prioritizing a single command solution as per the implementation guide.

# New Feature on Tigris: Fork Buckets Like You Fork Code
created: 2025-10-29, last updated: 2026-03-11, [Read more](https://community.fly.io/t/new-feature-on-tigris-fork-buckets-like-you-fork-code/26338)

`flyctl` doesn’t have support for forks and snapshots.
Tigris has a cli now, and it has support for forks and snapshots: tigris forks | Tigris Object Storage Documentation
`t3 forks create my-bucket my-fork`
`t3 snapshots take my-bucket my-snapshot`
The caveat here is that you need to enable snapshots when you create the bucket.
We don’t support enabling snapshots on an existing bucket yet (working on it!).
You can create a snapshot enabled bucket in the console or with the cli:
`t3 buckets create my-bucket --enable-snapshots`
...
The Tigris CLI can be used programmatically.
It works on your existing buckets created via the fly integration.

# Forking data for AI agents: The missing primitive for safe, ...
created: 2025-12-10, last updated: 2026-05-14, [Read more](https://www.aiacceleratorinstitute.com/forking-data-for-ai-agents-the-missing-primitive-for-safe-scalable-systems/)

This is the gap Tigris addresses with **whole-bucket snapshots** and **bucket forking**: capabilities absent from traditional object stores like S3.
...
This enables precise lineage, deterministic reads, and reproducible historical views; capabilities that traditional object stores cannot provide.
The result is a storage substrate that behaves more like a versioned data system than a bucket of files, but remains S3-compatible on the surface.
...
A fork:
- is created in milliseconds (zero-copy; metadata-only).
- inherits an exact snapshot of the parent bucket.
- provides isolated write space for agents or workflows.
- diverges safely without affecting the source dataset.
Agents running on a fork see a **stable, immutable snapshot**, ensuring deterministic reads.
All mutations occur in a private lineage, guaranteeing isolation.
...
The mechanisms that make forking feasible:
- **: point-in-time views resolved via “latest version ≤ timestamp,” ensuring deterministic reads.** Snapshots
...
They need **forking**, **snapshots**, and **versioned state**.
...
By introducing immutable storage, snapshots, and bucket forking as first-class primitives, Tigris provides the data foundation that agentic systems have been missing.
